clips.linkedin:
Your real competitor might not be another brand. It might be your customer doing nothing.

In this clip Hannah and I ask what your customer does instead of buying from you. For a cyclist it could be a current helmet with a cheap clip-on light, or not riding after dark at all. If the real alternative is staying at home, the job is giving people a reason to ride, and that changes the whole launch.

The research behind a question like that is a job you can hand to AI. Give it your reviews, forum threads and interview transcripts, and it returns findings with quotes, plus the groups the data does not cover.

The podcast voices are AI-generated, and mine is a clone of my own voice.

Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/what-is-marketing-basics/
clips.text: Instead of what? For a rider who wants to be seen on a dark evening, the alternative might be their current helmet with a cheap clip-on light. Or it might be not riding after dark at all. Those are very different competitors. And the second one's the interesting one, because that person isn't in anyone's market share figures. No. If the real alternative is staying at home, your job is to give them a reason to ride, not a reason to switch brands. That changes the whole launch.

clips.why: It names a single job for AI, says exactly what to give it and what comes back, and ends on the result with both James and Hannah speaking.

clips.linkedin:
Give AI your reviews, forum threads and interview transcripts and get ranked findings with quotes back.

Research synthesis takes the most hours, which is why teams used to skip it. Hannah and I go through the job in this clip from our episode on what marketing is.

Give it your review exports, forum threads and interview transcripts. Ask for the purchase triggers and the complaints, with the quotes behind each and how often it came up. You get back three or four findings with the evidence under each, and a list of the groups the data does not cover.

The prompt is in the show notes. The voices on the podcast are AI-generated, and mine is a clone of my own.

Full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/what-is-marketing-basics/
clips.text: Get AI on this. First, the research synthesis. That's the one that takes the most hours. Give it your review exports, a set of forum threads and your interview transcripts, and ask for the purchase triggers and the complaints, each with the quotes behind it and how often it came up. It hands back three or four findings with the evidence under each, and a list of the groups the data doesn't cover, like the people who aren't riding yet.
